entries.title: Exodus 38:8
segments:
Looking-glasses; mirrors of polished metal. 
 
  Which assembled; for religious purposes, and to unite in the worship of God. 
 
Religion has ever taken a strong and permanent hold upon the heart of woman; and while it has greatly elevated, adorned, and ennobled her character, increased her enjoyments, and extended her usefulness, it has been greatly promoted by her prayers, her example, her sacrifices, and her efforts.

entries.title: Exodus 38:18
segments: The height in the breadth; the height of the gate, or entrance, was equal to the breadth of the curtain, or hanging, which closed it.

entries.title: Exodus 38:21
segments: The sum; enumeration or statement of the various articles for the tabernacle.

entries.title: Exodus 38:24
segments:
Talents--shekels; a shekel was half an ounce avoir-dupois, and a talent equal to three thousand shekels, or ninety-three pounds and twelve ounces.  In value, a shekel was about fifty cents, and a talent of silver about fifteen hundred dollars.  A talent of gold was equal, it is supposed, to about twelve times that amount. 
 
However much property, at the direction of God, is devoted to the promotion of his glory, in the establishment and support of his worship, instead of being lost, as many suppose, it is employed to the greatest advantage, both to the possessors and to the world.
